svg.title: A profile's CPU-sample share overstates a parallel kernel's wall-clock share
svg.desc: A CPU profile attributes 50.6 percent of samples to the quantized dot product, which predicts that making it 1.12 times faster would speed a token up by 5.7 percent. The measured interleaved A/B gives 2.10 percent instead. Working backwards, that implies the kernel is only about 19 percent of wall clock. The gap is because the kernel is the fan-out-parallel part of a token, so it accrues roughly one CPU-second per core per wall-second while serial work accrues one.

g.text: the profile said 50.6%. the A/B said 19%.
one decode token · Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B int4 · Ryzen 7 3700X
CPU samples — what the profile shows
wall clock — what the measurement implies
the dot is the FAN-OUT-PARALLEL part of a token. It banks ~1 CPU-second
per core per wall-second; serial work banks 1. Sample share flatters it,
so 50.6% is a CEILING, not an estimate.
pre-registered as an upper bound BEFORE the A/B ran, so the gap read as expected
